exercise.name: Plank Shoulder Tap
steps: Start in a push-up position with your feet a little wider than hips.
Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder without rocking your hips.
Put the hand down and repeat with the other side.
exercise.one_line_summary: High plank on straight arms (hands under the shoulders), feet a little wider than the hips, body one straight line. One hand lifts and taps the opposite shoulder while the hips stay square and still, then returns. Rectus abdominis is the target (anti-extension + anti-rotation); obliques and the supporting front delt clearly work.

setup.target: Hands under the shoulders, arms straight.
setup.tolerance: hand within 0.05 m of under the shoulder

setup.target: On the toes, a little wider than hip-width (ankles ~0.34 m apart).
setup.why: Wider feet = more stable, hips rock less (S2); library step 1.

setup.target: Head to heels straight, abs braced, glutes squeezed.
setup.tolerance: hip within 0.04 m of the shoulder-ankle line

movement.measure: arm elev / plane / elbow in the torso frame
movement.start: 70.2 / 90 / 4 (hand on the floor under the shoulder)
movement.path: Lifts, crosses under the chin, taps the front-top of the opposite shoulder, returns.
movement.tolerance: hand within 0.05 m of the shoulder at the tap

movement.measure: pelvis turn about the long axis and hip height
movement.path: 'Keep the hips quiet' (S1): no rocking or rotating.
movement.tolerance: turn under 5 deg; hip height +-0.02 m

muscles.emg: No EMG study of shoulder taps found (searched). Close variants: planks with an unstable or moving demand (stir-the-pot) reach >61% MVIC RA, EO and IO (S3).
muscles.role: Holds the trunk straight against sagging while support drops to three points.
muscles.surface: Vertical bands down the front of the belly.

muscles.emg: Stir-the-pot plank EO and IO >61% MVIC; ball plank with hip extension 'very high' EO/IO (S3).
muscles.role: Stop the hips rotating when one hand lifts (anti-rotation, S1).

muscles.emg: Not measured for this move; serratus anterior 41-60% MVIC in the moving plank (S3).
muscles.role: The support shoulder holds more body weight on one arm.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: The pelvis twists toward the lifted hand.
Belly drops or the bottom pokes up.

sources.citation: National Academy of Sports Medicine. The plank: coaching, progressions and variations for every client (NASM blog).
sources.what_it_gave: Shoulder taps: 'keep the hips quiet', anti-rotation focus, needs a 30-45 s plank first.

sources.citation: Redefining Strength. Plank with Shoulder Taps (coaching article).
sources.what_it_gave: Hands under shoulders, feet wider for stability, tap the opposite shoulder, hips square; mistakes.

sources.citation: Youdas JW, Coleman KC, Holstad EE, Long SD, Veldkamp NL, Hollman JH. 2018. clip_check.target: within 0.05 m of the shoulder skin, not through it

clip_check.check: Hips square and level in both pictures
clip_check.target: pelvis turn < 5 deg; height change < 0.02 m

clip_check.check: Toes on the floor, feet a little wider than hips
